Klyro: a fintech identity

A next-generation money brand that needed to feel confident and fast without looking like every other digital bank. Here is the identity across print, product, social and outdoor.

My approach

Good brand design is rarely noticed. It is felt. Nobody walks away from an app saying the kerning was perfect, but they remember whether it felt trustworthy, quick and alive.

That is where I start every project. Before I draw a single mark, I ask what the brand should make someone feel in the first three seconds, and what it should still make them feel after three years. For Klyro the answer was confidence, speed and freedom, so the K was built from sharp, forward-leaning shards that suggest movement even when everything is standing still.

From there I build a system, not a logo. A mark only works if it survives a phone screen, a bank card, a street sign and a water bottle. So I test early and often: type pairings, color ratios, how the mark behaves at 16 pixels and at 6 feet tall. Every choice has to earn its place by making the brand clearer or more recognizable.

I care about research as much as craft. I look at who the audience is, what the category looks like and where everyone else is the same. In fintech that usually means blue and corporate. Choosing green, glass and bright lime was a deliberate move to stand apart while still signalling growth and money.

Motion is the final layer and the one that makes a brand feel real. Easing, timing and a small reveal on an app launch say more about personality than a paragraph of guidelines. I design with that in mind from the start, so the identity is ready to move across social, product and campaign work.

Finally, I design for the people who will live with the brand after I hand it over. That means clear rules, flexible assets and a story simple enough that a whole team can repeat it. If a brand is easy to use well, it stays consistent, and consistency is what turns a good-looking identity into one people trust.
